subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should core permanently expose this opt-in maintenance-timeout setting and shared SIGINT/SIGTERM cancellation behavior, while only fencing OpenClaw-owned side effects rather than cancelling arbitrary plugin work?
rationale: Tests and live proof support the implementation, but CI cannot decide whether a new permanent configuration knob, disabled-by-default recovery policy, partial plugin cancellation contract, and process-level signal ownership are the intended product semantics.

options.title: Approve the opt-in contract
options.body: Land the current design after refreshing it against main, explicitly documenting that timeout releases the lane and fences core state but does not forcibly cancel plugin-internal side effects.

options.title: Use a host-owned default
options.body: Replace the opt-in-only policy with an existing or new finite host default and provide fresh-install plus upgrade proof for legitimately long-running maintenance engines.

options.title: Require cooperative plugin cancellation
options.body: Pause this PR until the context-engine contract carries an AbortSignal or equivalent owner-defined cancellation seam, accepting the larger SDK and compatibility scope.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Land the current design after refreshing it against main, explicitly documenting that timeout releases the lane and fences core state but does not forcibly cancel plugin-internal side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the foundational context-engine lifecycle and is the strongest history-backed owner for a permanent core configuration and shutdown-policy decision.
